title: Reliable, antigen-specific immune tolerance

concept.text: The innovation would make the immune system durably accept a selected donor graft or antigen while retaining its ability to respond to infections and other threats. In transplantation, the intended outcome is sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression, achieved with acceptable treatment risks. Reduced drug requirements are meaningful progress, but do not by themselves demonstrate this complete capability.

The supplied clinical example pursues this goal through hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after solid-organ transplantation, using a graft depleted of naive T cells. This belongs to a broader approach involving donor-derived blood-forming cells and chimerism: the presence of donor-derived hematopoietic cells within the recipient. The engineering challenge includes cell preparation, conditioning, immune reprogramming and monitoring. Evidence from this approach concerns donor-associated transplant tolerance; it does not establish a general method for inducing tolerance to any chosen antigen.

significance.text: Reliable selective tolerance could substantially change transplantation by removing the need for broad, ongoing immunosuppression. The supplied report describes the association of chronic immunosuppression with infection, cardiovascular disease and cancer. If a tolerance-inducing intervention safely replaced maintenance treatment, it could reduce this treatment burden while preserving the graft. The net benefit would depend on whether the intervention and any conditioning introduce fewer or more manageable risks than the treatment they replace.

The essential advance would be selective acceptance, rather than simply weaker immune activity. A functioning graft accompanied by low donor-reactive responses and retained responses to unrelated challenges would be more informative than graft survival alone. The reported preservation of cytomegalovirus (CMV) responses in two patients is encouraging within that narrow scope, but cannot establish protection against infections generally or normal vaccine responses.

Conditional synthesis: a broadly usable tolerance platform could also make other replacement-tissue technologies more useful by addressing immune acceptance after implantation. Extension to autoimmune disease could be consequential, but accepting a donor graft and selectively suppressing a disease-causing response to self-antigens are distinct clinical problems. Each autoimmune application would require its own evidence of target specificity, disease control and preserved protective immunity.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a reproducible way to establish durable, selective tolerance across diverse recipients and transplant settings without dangerous conditioning or generalized immune impairment. The supplied article identifies conditioning requirements and restriction of many existing approaches to elective living-donor procedures as practical limitations. These constraints leave unresolved how to make treatment safe, broadly applicable and compatible with transplant circumstances beyond carefully selected protocols.

A central scientific and clinical barrier is determining when graft acceptance reflects a sufficiently selective and durable immune change to permit safe withdrawal of immunosuppression. Continued drug treatment complicates interpretation: rejection-free follow-up on monotherapy does not show that the same graft would remain protected without that treatment. The 2026 report explicitly calls for larger cohorts and prospective trials before withdrawal can be justified following its intervention.

Further work must connect immune measurements to clinical outcomes. Low donor-reactive responses need to be interpreted alongside responses to unrelated antigens, infection outcomes and the effects of ongoing medication. The supplied evidence does not establish a validated immune-test threshold that predicts safe withdrawal. Nor does it resolve how reliably this approach could tolerate an arbitrary chosen antigen or treat autoimmune disease.

current_state.text: The supplied article's literature summary reports that some kidney-transplant protocols using donor hematopoietic-cell treatment have enabled withdrawal of immunosuppression. It also describes continuing limitations involving conditioning and applicability, including reliance by many approaches on elective living-donor procedures. The underlying kidney studies were not supplied for direct inspection in the review, so this is a secondary account of prior progress rather than an independently assessed description of their outcomes or eligibility boundaries.

On 21 September 2026, Antonio Pérez-Martínez and colleagues published a two-patient case report of naive T cell-depleted hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation following solid-organ transplantation. The report described no signs of rejection after 6 and 5.2 years of follow-up, with recipients remaining on sirolimus or tacrolimus monotherapy. These observations demonstrate prolonged graft acceptance with minimized immunosuppression in two cases. They do not demonstrate complete drug withdrawal, establish that the intervention caused the outcomes, or show reliability across a diverse patient population.

The article contains an unresolved inconsistency in its immune-response reporting. Its abstract describes hyporesponsiveness to both donor and third-party cells, whereas the detailed results and the reviewed supplementary table show low donor responses with substantially greater third-party responses. For Patient 1, the detailed results report donor-response measurements of 0.79% and 0.94%, compared with third-party measurements of 7.27% and 10.5%. Supplementary Table 5's CD3+CD8+ CFSE-low row reports donor versus third-party values of 0.79% versus 7.27% for Patient 1 and 0.29% versus 44.7% for Patient 2. These measurements support a difference between donor and third-party responses within the reported assays, but do not establish normal immune competence relative to healthy controls or resolve the conflicting abstract wording.

CMV responses were retained in the reported experiments. This provides limited evidence that immune reactivity was not uniformly absent, but it does not establish broad infection protection, vaccine competence or drug-free tolerance. The two heterogeneous cases remain preliminary clinical evidence, and the authors state that their ultimate goal of a regimen without immunosuppression was not fully achieved.

The supplied review had complete main-article text in HTML and an 11-page PDF, but these are copies of the same study rather than independent confirmation. Figure images were not inspected. Supplementary extraction was partial: the relevant Table 5 headers and measurements were available, while Table 7's data were absent from the supplied extraction. These limits constrain interpretation of the full experimental record without negating the available clinical observations or Table 5 measurements.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: randomized studies across different transplant settings and diverse recipients would show sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression over prespecified long-term follow-up. Protocols would define withdrawal procedures, rejection surveillance, rescue treatment and acceptable treatment and conditioning risks in advance. These are proposed assessment criteria, not established consensus standards; the supplied evidence does not justify a particular universal follow-up duration or numerical success threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration of selectivity: donor-specific immune testing would be paired with unrelated-antigen responses, clinically observed infection outcomes and vaccine-response measurements. Together, these would test whether graft acceptance coexists with useful protective immunity. A single retained antiviral response or an isolated donor-reactivity assay would provide only part of that evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Donor-specific graft acceptance coexists with useful protective immunity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent teams and centers would reproduce the outcomes with sufficiently specified cell-processing, conditioning, treatment and monitoring procedures. Studies would report which recipient groups, donor relationships and organ types were included, where treatment failed, and whether its risks and logistics permit routine use. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions, rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproduce outcomes and report practical treatment boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed extension beyond transplantation: separate disease-specific trials would establish whether selected autoimmune responses can be controlled durably while protective immunity is retained. Success in donor-associated graft acceptance would not alone complete the broader chosen-antigen ambition.
completion_criteria.label: Disease-specific trials demonstrate durable autoimmune control with protective immunity

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BME-01, Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand, addresses organ supply, while BME-06, Long-term banking of transplantable human organs, addresses preservation and availability. BME-08 addresses immune acceptance after transplantation. These capabilities could complement one another, but making or storing an organ does not establish tolerance, and tolerance does not solve organ production or preservation.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-12, Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation, shares the problem of immune acceptance but concerns transplantation across species and has a broader completion burden. The supplied human transplant evidence does not establish tolerance to animal-derived organs or complete the animal-to-human transplantation concept.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-05, Programmable living medicines that sense and respond inside the body, overlaps with BME-08 when engineered cells are used to regulate immunity. Its defining capability is sensing and responding within the body; BME-08's defining outcome is durable, selective tolerance. BME-02, Programmable delivery of genetic therapies to most tissues, could offer enabling delivery methods, but successful delivery alone would not establish immune tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-16, Long-lived tissue-integrated interfaces for implants, and BME-13, Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement, both concern sustained compatibility between a therapeutic device and the body. Antigen-specific graft tolerance would not by itself solve the full biological, material and functional requirements of implanted interfaces or artificial organs. BME-17, Minimally invasive assembly of functional tissue inside the body, could intersect with tolerance when introduced tissue presents immune targets, while retaining its distinct challenge of assembling functional tissue.

unresolved_issues: The abstract's characterization of third-party hyporesponsiveness conflicts with the detailed results and supplementary Table 5. The supplied material contains no author clarification resolving it.
The available immune-response measurements do not establish normal-control equivalence, broad infection protection or vaccine competence.
Whether recipients treated with this intervention can safely discontinue maintenance immunosuppression remains unestablished.
The underlying kidney-protocol studies were not supplied for direct review, leaving their detailed outcomes, eligibility conditions and risks unassessed here.
Figure images were not inspected, and supplementary Table 7 data were absent from the supplied extraction; their implications cannot be resolved from the provided review.
Reliability across diverse recipients, transplant settings, arbitrary chosen antigens and autoimmune diseases remains unestablished.
Immune memory and loss of established tolerance were not retained as evidence-established barriers because the supplied source does not substantiate those original assertions.
The supplied freshness record is empty, so the review does not establish whether the September 2026 report represents the latest available evidence.

brief.title: Lasting immune acceptance without losing protection
possible: People receiving a donor organ could keep it working without lifelong anti-rejection drugs. Their immune system would accept the transplant while still responding to infections and vaccines.

The broader goal is to stop an immune attack on a chosen target without weakening other defenses. This could also help people with autoimmune diseases, in which the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues.
why: Transplant recipients could avoid the burden of ongoing immune suppression and its associated risks, including infection, cardiovascular disease and cancer.
Reliable immune acceptance could also make implanted replacement tissues more useful by addressing rejection.

sources.showed: A small case report described lasting organ acceptance after patients received blood-forming stem cells from their organ donor. Patients continued taking low-dose anti-rejection medicine.
sources.quote: Several years later, both patients remain stable, have no signs of organ rejection, and only need very low doses of anti-rejection medicines.
sources.cited_for: Donor blood-forming cells may help reduce the need for anti-rejection drugs.
sources.not_established: The report did not demonstrate acceptance without drugs or establish that the treatment caused the outcomes.

sources.who: Stephan Busque and colleagues at Stanford University
sources.showed: Selected kidney recipients with closely matched living donors stopped anti-rejection drugs after receiving donor blood-forming cells. Less closely matched recipients experienced rejection when treatment stopped.
sources.quote: No evidence of rejection was observed in all surveillance graft biopsies obtained from mixed chimeric patients withdrawn from IS drugs, and none developed graft-versus-host disease.
sources.cited_for: Drug-free kidney acceptance is possible when donor and recipient blood-forming cells coexist, a state called mixed chimerism.
sources.not_established: Success in selected matched recipients does not establish reliable acceptance across donor matches or organ types.

sources.showed: Three kidney recipients with closely matched sibling donors stopped anti-rejection drugs and retained vaccine responses. Donated immune cells did not attack their bodies, a complication called graft-versus-host disease.
sources.quote: No rejection or graft-versus-host disease occurred.
sources.cited_for: A separate team reproduced drug-free kidney acceptance with evidence of retained vaccine responses.
sources.not_established: The small sibling-donor trial does not establish broad applicability or protection against infections generally.

sources.showed: A kidney recipient later rejected the organ despite a low donor response in a mixed lymphocyte reaction (MLR), a laboratory immune test.
sources.quote: At that time, the MLR still showed a low response to the donor.
sources.cited_for: Weak laboratory responses to donor cells do not guarantee lasting acceptance after drug withdrawal.
sources.not_established: The case does not establish a reliable test for deciding when anti-rejection drugs can safely stop.

sources.who: Ciarán P Kelly and colleagues, on behalf of the TAK-101 Study Group
sources.showed: In a small randomized trial, TAK-101, tiny particles carrying gluten protein, reduced gluten-triggered immune activity in celiac disease (CeD), an immune disorder triggered by gluten.
sources.quote: TAK-101 was well tolerated and prevented gluten-induced immune activation in CeD.
sources.cited_for: Treatment can reduce an immune response to a specific target beyond transplantation.
sources.not_established: The trial did not establish lasting disease control, clear protection from intestinal damage or broadly preserved protective immunity.

shown: Stanford researchers achieved complete anti-rejection drug withdrawal in 24 selected kidney recipients with closely matched donors. They combined kidney transplantation with donor blood-forming cells.

A small Zurich trial reproduced drug-free kidney acceptance and found retained vaccine responses. Pérez-Martínez and colleagues reported prolonged acceptance after other organ transplants, but their patients continued anti-rejection medicine.
missing: Treatment has yet to work reliably across diverse recipients and transplant settings with acceptable risks from preparatory treatment.
No validated immune-test threshold predicts when anti-rejection drugs can safely stop.
Lasting control of selected autoimmune responses, together with preserved protective immunity, remains to be demonstrated.

milestones.label: Transplants keep working without anti-rejection drugs
milestones.explanation: Randomized studies across diverse recipients and transplant settings would have to show lasting organ function without rejection or ongoing drugs, at acceptable treatment risk. This would establish reliable drug-free acceptance.

milestones.label: Transplant acceptance preserves useful immune defenses
milestones.explanation: Donor-response tests, unrelated immune responses, infection outcomes and vaccine responses would have to show preserved protection alongside acceptance. This would distinguish selective acceptance from broad immune weakening.

milestones.label: Independent centers reproduce results and define treatment limits
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to reproduce outcomes with clearly described procedures and report eligible patients, failures, risks and logistics. This would establish where routine treatment is practical.

milestones.label: Autoimmune disease stays controlled while immune protection remains
milestones.explanation: Separate disease-specific trials would have to show lasting control of selected autoimmune responses while preserving protective immunity. This would establish whether selective acceptance extends beyond donor organs.

uncertain: It remains unclear how much donor and recipient blood-forming cells must coexist, and for how long, to sustain acceptance.
The Pérez-Martínez report conflicts internally about responses to unrelated cells, leaving the selectivity of its immune effects uncertain.
The follow-up duration and success rate needed to judge reliable tolerance across settings remain open.

page.title: Donor-specific transplantation tolerance
page.definition: Treatment establishes acceptance of a donor organ without ongoing immunosuppressive drugs while preserving immunity to unrelated antigens, the molecular targets recognized by immune cells.

goal.need: The United States performed 48,149 organ transplants in 2024, including 27,759 kidney and 11,458 liver transplants, according to preliminary OPTN data. NIAID identifies infection, malignancy and atherosclerosis as risks of systemic immunosuppression and makes donor-specific tolerance a goal for avoiding that treatment burden.

figures.caption: United States transplant procedures in 2024: preliminary OPTN counts.
figures.note: Procedure counts describe transplantation volume, not eligibility for tolerance protocols.

statements.body: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
statements.quote: Tolerance induction strategies aim to selectively block or prevent deleterious immune responses, while leaving protective immunity intact.
achieve the complete and planned withdrawal of all immunosuppression while maintaining the healthy function of the graft organ.
statements.context: The stated primary goal of the network's interventional transplantation studies.

completion.title: A recipient maintains a drug-free functioning graft and immunity to non-donor antigens.
completion.criterion: Following a tolerance-inducing intervention, clinical assessment, laboratory tests and histology demonstrate normal and/or stable donor-organ function after complete withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs, with concurrent immunocompetence to non-donor antigens. ITN specifies no minimum follow-up duration, population success fraction or immune-assay cutoff.
completion.set_by: Immune Tolerance Network, Strategic Plan: Transplantation, Clinical Objectives, together with its Research Focus - Transplantation goal of complete drug withdrawal.
completion.threshold_quote: normal and/or stable allograft function, in the absence of generalized immunosuppression with concurrent immunocompetence to non-donor antigens.
completion.basis: Clinical proof of concept was reported on 31 January 2022 in 3 HLA-identical sibling kidney recipients: 4 years, 19 months and 8 months off drugs, respectively, without rejection or graft-versus-host disease. All 3 had vaccine-induced SARS-CoV-2 antibodies; 2 had detectable vaccine-specific T-cell responses. These observations establish a selected-patient demonstration, without a general success rate or evidence of protection against every pathogen.

milestones.title: A treated animal accepts donor tissue and rejects third-party tissue without maintenance immunosuppression.
milestones.criterion: The animal retains its organ graft, accepts a second donor graft and rejects an unrelated donor's graft after maintenance drugs stop. Kidney: skin-graft testing supported tolerance in 5 of 6 long-surviving rhesus recipients in 1997. Heart/kidney: 1 of 5 challenged cynomolgus recipients accepted donor skin indefinitely; all 5 rejected third-party skin in the 2025 report. Lung: 1 recipient in a 6-monkey study accepted donor skin for over 134 days and rejected third-party skin in 20 days in 2015.
milestones.set_by: Experimental transplantation convention, stated by Ezekian and colleagues in Contemporary Strategies and Barriers to Transplantation Tolerance.
milestones.threshold_quote: a second graft from the same donor should be accepted, whereas a graft from a third-party donor should be rejected.

milestones.title: An organ recipient has no rejection or graft-versus-host disease at 6 and 12 months.
milestones.criterion: Following donor hematopoietic-cell transplantation, assess absence of organ rejection and graft-versus-host disease at 6 and 12 months. The latter is donor immune cells attacking recipient tissues. Zurich reported no such events in 3 HLA-identical kidney recipients. A report published on 21 September 2026 described 2 recipients, one multivisceral including intestine and kidney and one kidney-only, without rejection or graft-versus-host disease after 6 and 5.2 years, respectively; both continued immunosuppressive monotherapy.
milestones.set_by: University Hospital Zurich, NCT00365846 secondary endpoints; written for HLA-identical sibling kidney and hematopoietic-cell transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: absence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after 6 and 12 months, absence of renal allograft rejection at 6 and 12 months

milestones.title: An organ recipient maintains graft function for at least 1 year without immunosuppressive drugs.
milestones.criterion: Maintain stable graft function without clinical rejection or overt immunodeficiency for at least 1 year after complete drug withdrawal. Kidney: Stanford withdrew drugs in 24 of 29 fully HLA-matched recipients; 23 of 24 remained rejection-free during follow-up of up to 10 years, although 4 resumed drugs. Liver: LIFT found biopsy-defined tolerance in 13 of 80 withdrawal participants at 12 months. Intestine: 1 recipient remained drug-free for 5 years with donor hyporesponsiveness and antiviral responses; withdrawal was spontaneous, not a planned induction.
milestones.set_by: Clinical operational-tolerance convention summarized by Massart and colleagues; minimum duration documented for kidney transplantation. Liver evidence additionally uses LIFT biopsy criteria.
milestones.threshold_quote: All authors agreed upon a strict minimal period of 1 year without immunosuppression before evoking tolerance.

milestones.title: An organ recipient remains off all immunosuppressive drugs for more than 2 years in a randomized trial.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate sustained drug withdrawal in a randomized clinical trial. In NCT03363945, adults receiving kidneys from two-haplotype HLA-matched living siblings received MDR-101 donor cells or standard care. Withdrawal was conditional on donor blood-cell chimerism of at least 5%. Of 20 treated recipients and 10 controls, 19 treated recipients stopped all drugs around 1 year after transplantation and 15 remained off for more than 2 years; 4 restarted. This endpoint establishes functional tolerance without directly testing unrelated immunity.
milestones.set_by: Medeor Therapeutics, NCT03363945 primary endpoint, reported by Kaufman and colleagues in 2025; written for HLA-matched living-sibling kidney transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

not_found: No common completion test spanning donor-graft tolerance and tolerance to arbitrary autoimmune targets was located.
The 2025 MDR-101 publisher full text and ClinicalTrials.gov outcome fields were not readable; the authors' institutional abstract was accessible.
No prospective human heart or lung tolerance-induction result meeting the full ITN objective was located.
